out.subject: Alloy bar pricing – committed quantity and fixed-price terms
out.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of your cost drivers. I appreciate the transparency; alongside the annual movements you cited, please consider the recent alloy-index figures below when reviewing your price.

Our proposed term sheet is EUR 5.10 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract without an index clause. It includes a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg throughout the full contract term, not merely a forecast.

I have attached the shared monthly forecast to support your planning. The forecast provides the demand profile; the quantity commitment is part of the proposed term sheet.

What price can you offer for this committed quantity on a fixed-price basis?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Propose a committed-quantity fixed-price package, supported by the shared forecast and verified alloy-index evidence, while directly addressing the supplier's cost-driver explanation.

out.subject: Revised terms for stainless bar supply
out.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for reviewing the data and accepting payment at 90 days net. I also appreciate your willingness to agree to a 24-month term, subject to an alloy-index clause.

To answer your volume question: our proposed term sheet commits to 23700 kg a year throughout the full 24 months. This is our full requirement, binding rather than indicative; we cannot increase that quantity.

I have noted your position on the AS-14404 clause. For now, our revised proposal remains without an index clause, at EUR 5.13 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract.

Please also consider our existing purchase orders with you for this bar, as documented below, when reviewing the revised price. What further price improvement can you offer on this committed package?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Answers the volume question explicitly, acknowledges the accepted payment term and conditional contract duration, and introduces purchase-order evidence while modestly revising the clause-free proposal.

out.subject: Re: Bar supply – revised committed package
out.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for confirming your terms and checking the purchase-order history. I understand that your offer requires an AS-14404 clause over the 24-month term; I have noted that condition, although our revised sheet remains on a fixed-price basis for your review.

You also named PPI-C2431 as a main cost driver. Please consider the recent figures below alongside the annual movements in your calculation.

Our revised proposal is EUR 5.18 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract without an index clause. The sheet includes a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg throughout the contract term.

What is your best price for this committed package after reviewing the additional cost-driver data? Thank you also for offering your wider range; this enquiry remains focused on the bar requirement.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

out.subject: Bar supply: revised package and price clarification
out.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for taking the recent cost-driver data into account and improving your offer. I understand that you require an AS-14404 clause for a 24-month contract, and I respect your position on sharing further cost detail.

For your review, our revised term sheet is EUR 5.21 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract without an index clause. It includes a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg throughout the contract term.

Please give us your best price on this revised fixed-price package. Your latest e-mail also lists EUR 5.20 per kg in the main offer but refers to EUR 5.30 per kg later in the text. Please confirm which price applies to your AS-14404 offer without a deadband, so that the price and clause are unambiguous.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Move the fixed-price proposal modestly forward while retaining the quantity, payment and duration terms. Acknowledge the supplier's index condition and request clarification of its inconsistent quoted prices; do not repeat previously submitted claims.
